purpose: When does a calibration trace cross its target level?
meaning: The discriminant separates two distinct real crossings, one double root and no real roots. The model classifies its exact represented inputs, then evaluates root positions numerically using a cancellation-resistant quadratic calculation.

definition.setting: A calibration trace curves relative to a target line. The leading coefficient fixes the upward curvature, the linear coefficient tilts the trace, and the constant moves it vertically. Drag the constant offset and watch two crossings meet in a tangency before the trace rises clear of the target.
conditions: The leading coefficient is between 0.5 and 2; the other coefficients lie between −4 and 4. Only real solutions are drawn. A double root is one distinct real solution. Exact binary-input discriminant sign is separate from approximate root positions; unresolved numerical distinctions report a precision failure. The fixed drawing window can crop a root.
